/-!
# Erdős Problem 372

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/372](https://www.erdosproblems.com/372)

Conjectured by Erdős and Pomerance. Proved by Balog, who showed the stronger quantitative result
that this holds for $\gg \sqrt{x}$ many $n\leq x$, for all large $x$.
-/

namespace Erdos372

/--
Let $P(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$. There are infinitely many $n$ such that
$P(n)>P(n+1)>P(n+2)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_372 :
    {n : ℕ | Nat.maxPrimeFac n > Nat.maxPrimeFac (n + 1) ∧
      Nat.maxPrimeFac (n + 1) > Nat.maxPrimeFac (n + 2)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos372

reformulations.difference: Lean ranges over all natural numbers and uses a totalized largest-prime-factor function, without explicitly restricting to n > 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n > 1, Nat.maxPrimeFac is precisely the greatest prime divisor. Its exceptional values are P(0)=0 and P(1)=1; neither 0 nor 1 satisfies the first strict inequality, since P(2)=2. Thus the solution set is exactly equal to the set obtained by adding 1 < n. The set equality and the resulting equivalence of infinitude statements were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
